text: Averaging labels from an ensemble of three weak supervisors (gpt2-large) to train a mistral-7b student yields a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.89 with a standard error of 0.10 across 8 seeds, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.39. The margin over the baseline exceeds two standard errors of the PGR estimate, so the ensemble-averaging setup can be characterized as an improvement over the single-supervisor baseline rather than noise. In absolute terms, the weak supervisors reach 0.57 accuracy, the transfer-trained strong student reaches 0.87 (standard error 0.03), and the strong model's ceiling accuracy is 0.91, so the student lands between its weak teachers and its own fully supervised performance. Caveats worth noting: no standard error is reported for the baseline PGR, weak and strong accuracies are given without uncertainty estimates, and the results come from a single model pair with ensemble size 3, so generality across scales and architectures is untested.
